classification.difficultyReason: Converts supplied table inputs into two reciprocal graphs, then tracks how the negative numerator reverses branch positions and the side from which each graph approaches zero.

content.prompt: Plot these graphs on the same axis.

spec.description: Portrait coordinate grid with integer grid lines and ticks, x from −4 to 4 and y from −10 to 10. Both axes have arrowheads at both ends; zero is unlabelled.
spec.mathematics: Common coordinate frame for y=2/x and y=-2/x; explicit grid step 1 on both axes.
spec.answerVisibility: Blank coordinate grid in Questions; completed curves are retained separately as answer content.

inlines.text: Divide 2 or −2 by each nonzero x-value. At
both expressions are undefined. Plot the defined points and join smooth branches approaching the axes.

spec.description: Complete common-axis answer graph. Four reciprocal branches have continuation arrowheads. Blue solid and red dashed series distinguish the two equations; labels are added outside the coordinate frame.
spec.mathematics: y=2/x in quadrants I and III; y=-2/x in quadrants II and IV. Axes x=0 and y=0 are their common asymptotes. Integer grid step 1; x range −4 to 4 and y range −10 to 10.
spec.presentationRepair: Retain each y-scale value beside its actual axis tick. Choose the nearby clear side using the plotted branch signs; use small offsets only where both reciprocal signs are plotted.

children.prompt: Describe their differences in terms of:

answer.worked: As positive $x$ increases, both graphs approach $y=0$. For $y=\frac2x$, the values remain positive, so the graph approaches from above. For $y=-\frac2x$, the values remain negative, so it approaches from below.

As negative $x$ decreases without bound, both graphs approach $y=0$. For $y=\frac2x$, the values remain negative, so the graph approaches from below. For $y=-\frac2x$, the values remain positive, so it approaches from above.
